Genetic Technologies — additional terms

insert

Meaning

The DNA segment placed into a vector or other specified DNA construct.

Word structure

A noun for the DNA segment placed into a vector; insertion names the act or sequence change.

What it does

The chosen DNA segment adds a sequence to the construct for the intended study or expression task.

Related ideas

chloroplast DNA · gene therapy · genetic testing

Common confusion

An insert's presence does not prove its orientation or expression is correct.

Retrieve the idea

What check would distinguish having an insert from having the intended insert in the intended orientation?

Molecular evidence

Meaning

Polymerase chain reaction; a laboratory method that uses primers and repeated temperature cycles to amplify a selected DNA region.

Word structure

Initialism for polymerase chain reaction. Chain reaction describes repeated amplification, not protein translation.

Repeated denaturation, primer annealing and extension amplify a primer-bounded region.

gel electrophoresis · fragment size · ladder · nuclear DNA

PCR amplifies DNA; it does not itself establish a sequence's biological function.

How do primer-binding sites determine which region is amplified?

Molecular evidence

gel electrophoresis

Meaning

A method that separates charged molecules through a gel, commonly resolving DNA fragments mainly by length.

Word structure

Electro- concerns electricity and -phoresis movement; gel specifies the medium through which charged fragments migrate.

What it does

Charged fragments move through a matrix, with length affecting migration under the specified conditions.

PCR · fragment size · ladder · nuclear DNA

A DNA band's position does not reveal its full base sequence.

Why can equal-length DNA fragments share a band despite different sequences?

Molecular evidence

fragment size

The length of a DNA fragment, commonly measured in base pairs.

Word structure

Size here is usually sequence length in bases or base pairs, not the darkness of a gel band.

Length in bases or base pairs allows comparisons with a size reference.

Related ideas

PCR · gel electrophoresis · ladder · nuclear DNA

Common confusion

Size is not the same as DNA amount in a band.

Distinguish the information suggested by band position and band intensity.

Molecular evidence

ladder

Meaning

A set of DNA fragments of known sizes used as a gel reference.

Word structure

A visual metaphor for a set of reference fragments; its known sizes support comparisons on a gel.

Known fragment lengths provide comparison points for estimating sample fragment size.

PCR · gel electrophoresis · fragment size · nuclear DNA

Common confusion

A ladder is a reference, not another unknown sample.

How would you estimate the size of a band falling between two ladder bands?

DNA contained in the nucleus, including the chromosomes used in ordinary nuclear inheritance models.

Genetic Technologies — additional terms

chloroplast DNA

Meaning

DNA contained in chloroplasts, useful alongside other sequences when comparing related organisms.

Chloroplast identifies the organelle carrying the DNA, not a green base or a chlorophyll gene alone.

Plastid sequences provide an additional source of inherited markers in photosynthetic lineages.

Why can comparing chloroplast and nuclear markers provide different lineage information?

An analysis of appropriately aligned nucleotide sequences to identify similarities and differences.

Aligned homologous positions reveal similarities and differences relevant to the comparison question.

Why must sequences be appropriately aligned before counting differences?

Genetic Technologies — additional terms

gene therapy

Meaning

An approach intended to treat a condition by altering genetic material or its delivery/expression in relevant cells.

Word structure

Therapy names a treatment approach; gene specifies intervention involving genetic material, not guaranteed cure.

A proposed intervention changes genetic material or its expression in relevant cells to address a condition.

Common confusion

Changing some target cells does not imply correction in every cell or guaranteed benefit.

What delivery and target-cell limitations must accompany a gene-therapy claim?

Analysis of genetic material to investigate a specified variant or question, with limits determined by the method.

Resources

Glossary and Data

Use these definitions for reference. The required lessons introduce terms where you first need them.

3-prime

The end/direction associated with the sugar's 3′ carbon; polymerases extend a strand at its available 3′ hydroxyl.

Review: Nucleotides and direction
5-prime

The end/direction associated with the sugar's 5′ carbon in a nucleic-acid strand.

Review: Nucleotides and direction
5-prime to 3-prime

The direction in which a new DNA or RNA strand is extended by adding nucleotides to its 3′ end.

Review: Nucleotides and direction
9:3:3:1 ratio

The expected phenotype ratio from AaBb × AaBb when the two loci assort independently, each has complete dominance, and the model assumes ordinary segregation and equal survival of the offspring classes.

A site

The ribosome site that usually receives an incoming amino-acid-carrying tRNA as a protein chain is lengthened.

ABO

A human blood-group system controlled by multiple alleles in which IA and IB are codominant and i is recessive.

Review: Codominance and multiple alleles
ABO blood group

A human blood-group system controlled by multiple alleles in which IA and IB are codominant and i is recessive.

actionability

The degree to which a test result can support a useful, evidence-based decision or intervention.

addition rule

A probability rule for mutually exclusive alternatives: add the probabilities of the separate outcomes.

affected

A pedigree label indicating the specified phenotype; it is not a judgment about the person.

Review: Inheritance modes and notation
allele

One of two or more DNA-sequence versions at a gene or locus.

Review: DNA packaging
allele pair

The two allele copies at a locus in a diploid individual, one associated with each homologue.

Review: Segregation
allele product

An RNA or protein output associated with a gene variant, contributing to how a genotype affects a trait.

Review: Inheritance language
alternation of generations

A life cycle alternating multicellular haploid and multicellular diploid stages.

alternative model

A different explanation that can be compared against the same observations.

Review: Autosomal hypotheses
alternative splicing

Production of different mature RNA transcripts by combining exons from the same pre-mRNA in different ways.

amino acid

One of the small chemical building blocks joined into a protein chain.

Review: Making RNA
analytical validity

How accurately and reliably a test detects the molecular feature it claims to measure.

anaphase

The division stage when separated chromosomes or chromatids move toward opposite poles.

Review: Preparing to separate
anaphase I

The meiotic stage when homologous chromosomes move toward opposite poles while sisters remain associated.

Review: First meiotic division
aneuploidy

A chromosome number with one or more individual chromosomes added or missing rather than a complete set change.

Review: Reading karyotypes
anticodon

A three-nucleotide sequence on tRNA that pairs with a complementary mRNA codon.

Review: Reading the genetic code
antigen

A molecular feature recognized by an immune receptor or antibody; ABO antigens occur on red-blood-cell surfaces.

antiparallel

Describes DNA strands running in opposite 5-prime-to-3-prime directions.

Review: Nucleotides and direction
apoptosis

A regulated form of cell death that removes selected cells without the uncontrolled rupture typical of severe injury.

asexual reproduction

Reproduction from one parent without gamete fusion, usually producing genetically similar descendants except for mutation.

Review: Comparing divisions
autosomal

Located on, or inherited through, an autosome.

Review: Reading karyotypes
autosomal dominant

A model in which a trait-associated allele on an autosome is expressed in the heterozygote.

Review: Inheritance modes and notation
autosomal recessive

A model in which two copies of a trait-associated autosomal allele are required for the specified phenotype.

Review: Inheritance modes and notation
autosome

A chromosome other than a sex chromosome in the classification being used.

Review: Reading karyotypes
backbone

The connected sugar-phosphate chain of a nucleic-acid strand.

Review: Nucleotides and direction
bacterial conjugation

Transfer of DNA from a donor bacterium to a recipient through direct cell contact; transfer itself does not make an additional cell.

Review: Sexual and asexual reproduction
banding pattern

The reproducible light-and-dark chromosome pattern used to identify chromosomes and some structural changes in a karyotype.

base

One of the information-bearing chemical units in DNA or RNA; ordinary DNA uses A, T, G and C, while RNA usually uses U in place of T.

Review: DNA packaging
base pairing

Specific hydrogen-bond pairing of adenine with thymine or uracil and guanine with cytosine.

Review: Nucleotides and direction
benefit

A favourable outcome for a specified person, group or system, evaluated using stated criteria.

Review: Evidence and applications
binary fission

Asexual cell reproduction in which one cell copies its genetic material and divides into two cells.

Review: Sexual and asexual reproduction
blinding

Keeping observers unaware of sample identity or treatment to reduce expectation bias.

blunt end

A double-stranded DNA end with no single-stranded overhang.

branch method

A probability method that multiplies along sequential branches and adds mutually exclusive final pathways.

cancer

A group of diseases involving abnormal cell growth caused by accumulated genetic and cellular-control changes in context.

carrier

In simple recessive inheritance, a heterozygous individual who has one recessive allele and usually lacks the associated phenotype.

Review: Probability rules
cell cycle

The ordered sequence of growth, DNA replication, chromosome separation, and division in a typical dividing cell.

cell plate

A plant-cell structure formed during cytokinesis that develops into new membranes and a separating cell wall.

Review: Finishing cell division
cell-cycle regulation

Control of when and whether a cell proceeds through growth, replication and division.

Review: Control and division
centimorgan

A genetic-map unit: one centimorgan corresponds to about one percent recombination over a short chromosome interval. It is not a fixed physical length of DNA.

centromere

A chromosome region involved in joining sister chromatids and attaching the chromosome to the cell-division machinery.

Review: Sets and copies
chain of custody

A documented record of who collected, handled, transferred, stored, and analyzed a sample.

Chargaff

Erwin Chargaff, whose measurements established important base-composition relationships in DNA.

Review: Evidence for hereditary material
Chargaff's rules

The observed DNA base relationships that adenine approximately equals thymine and guanine approximately equals cytosine in double-stranded DNA.

checkpoint

A regulatory control point that can delay cell-cycle progression when conditions or molecular events are unsuitable.

Review: Control and division
chiasma

The visible physical connection between homologous chromosomes associated with an earlier crossing-over event.

Review: Pairing and exchange
chloroplast DNA

DNA contained in chloroplasts, useful alongside other sequences when comparing related organisms.

Review: Genetic evidence and relatedness
chromatid

One DNA-protein copy of a replicated chromosome; joined sister chromatids separate during cell division.

chromatin

DNA together with associated proteins that package and regulate genetic material in the nucleus.

Review: DNA packaging
chromosome

An organized DNA–protein structure. Before copying, it contains one DNA molecule. After copying, it contains two attached copies; when they separate, each is counted as a chromosome.

Review: DNA packaging
cleavage furrow

The inward pinching of an animal cell membrane during cytokinesis.

Review: Finishing cell division
clinical validity

How well a test result predicts or associates with a clinical condition in the intended population.

clone

A cell or organism descended asexually from one source and therefore highly similar genetically, though not necessarily identical in phenotype.

Review: Sexual and asexual reproduction
cloning

Producing genetically closely related cells or organisms from a source lineage; environmental and later genetic differences can remain.

Review: Evidence and applications
coding strand

The DNA strand whose sequence matches the RNA transcript except that DNA has thymine where RNA has uracil.

Review: Selecting a template
codominance

An inheritance pattern in which both alleles in a heterozygote contribute distinct detectable products or traits.

Review: Incomplete dominance
codon

A three-nucleotide mRNA sequence that specifies an amino acid or a translation start or stop signal.

Review: Checking a sequence claim
communication

Presenting a question, method, evidence and explanation clearly enough for another reader to assess them.

Review: Observation and simulation
complementarity

Specific hydrogen-bond pairing of adenine with thymine or uracil and guanine with cytosine.

Review: The double helix
complementary

Able to match through the specified base-pairing relationships, such as A–T and G–C in DNA.

Review: Evidence for hereditary material
complementary base pairing

Specific hydrogen-bond pairing of adenine with thymine or uracil and guanine with cytosine.

complete dominance

An inheritance pattern in which the heterozygote has the same scored phenotype as one homozygote.

conditional probability

The probability of an event after specified information or a condition is taken into account.

Review: Probability rules
consent

An informed and voluntary agreement to a specified use or procedure; one agreement does not authorize every later use.

Review: Reading karyotypes
continuous variation

A range of measured trait values, often influenced by several genes and environmental conditions.

Review: Genes and environment
control

A comparison condition or regulated variable used to make an investigation interpretable.

Review: Evidence and applications
controlled variable

A factor intentionally kept consistent to help isolate the effect being tested in a comparison.

converging evidence

Independent evidence types that support the same bounded explanation.

Crick

Francis Crick, who worked with James Watson on a model of DNA structure informed by experimental evidence.

Review: Evidence for hereditary material
crossing over

Reciprocal DNA exchange between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes during meiotic prophase I.

Review: Pairing and exchange
cyclin

A regulatory protein whose changing concentration helps control cyclin-dependent kinase activity during the cell cycle.

cyclin-dependent kinase

An enzyme whose activity depends on a cyclin partner and other controls; it adds phosphate groups to target proteins involved in cell-cycle transitions.

cytokinesis

Physical division of a cell's cytoplasm into daughter cells.

Review: Interphase
Daphnia

A genus of small aquatic crustaceans used here to compare environmentally influenced sexual and asexual reproductive strategies.

Review: Sexual and asexual reproduction
data sovereignty

The right of a people or community to govern collection, ownership, access, interpretation, and use of data about them.

daughter chromosome

A former sister chromatid counted as a separate chromosome after sister separation.

Review: Sets and copies
daughter strand

A newly synthesized DNA strand produced during replication.

Review: Semiconservative replication
deletion

Loss of one or more nucleotides or of a chromosome segment.

Review: From sequence to function
deoxyribose

The five-carbon sugar found in DNA nucleotides.

Review: Nucleotides and direction
dependent variable

The measured response used to evaluate an investigation's prediction.

dihybrid cross

A genetic cross that follows inheritance at two loci.

diploid

Having two chromosome sets, conventionally written 2n.

Review: Sets and copies
diploid-dominant

A life cycle in which the main multicellular body is diploid and the haploid stage is reduced. In the animal pattern, the haploid cells are gametes.

direction

The stated orientation of a process or strand; nucleic-acid answers require 5′ and 3′ labels.

Review: Nucleotides and direction
DNA

Deoxyribonucleic acid: a long molecule whose sequence of chemical units carries hereditary information.

Review: DNA packaging
DNA ligase

An enzyme that seals breaks in a DNA sugar-phosphate backbone by forming phosphodiester bonds.

DNA polymerase

An enzyme that builds DNA by adding complementary nucleotides to an existing 3-prime end and often proofreads the product.

Review: Enzymes and direction
DNA profile

A pattern of DNA markers used to compare biological samples; it is probabilistic evidence, not a complete identity record.

DNA replication

Copying DNA so that each resulting double-stranded molecule has one original strand and one newly made strand.

Review: Sets and copies
DNA sequencing

Determining the order of nucleotides in a DNA molecule or selected DNA region.

dominant

Describes an allele whose scored phenotype appears in a heterozygote under specified conditions.

Review: Inheritance language
dose

The amount of an agent delivered or received, with its units and exposure conditions stated.

Review: Effects on gene products
double crossover

Two crossing-over events within the chromosome interval being studied.

double helix

The two-stranded helical structure of DNA with antiparallel sugar-phosphate backbones and paired bases.

driver mutation

A DNA sequence change that contributes to a cell's cancer-related growth or survival advantage.

E site

The ribosome exit site for a tRNA no longer carrying an amino acid or growing protein chain.

elongation

The stage in which a growing RNA or polypeptide chain is extended.

Review: Adaptors and peptide bonds
environment

The physical, biological and other surrounding conditions relevant to an organism or process.

Review: Twins and early development
environmental influence

An effect of surrounding conditions on development, expression or performance of an organism.

Review: Genes and environment
epigenetic

Describes stable or regulated changes in gene activity that do not require changing the DNA base sequence.

evidence

Observations or results used to evaluate a claim, together with their method and limitations.

Review: Reading karyotypes
evidence scale

The biological level and measurement context to which an observation belongs, such as molecule, cell, organism, family, or population.

exon

A transcript segment retained in a mature RNA after splicing, though not every exon segment is protein-coding.

Review: Processing and expression
expected count

The number predicted for a category by a specified probability model and total sample size.

Review: Controlled crosses and evidence
experimental control

A comparison or controlled condition that helps isolate an interpretation of an experimental result.

Review: Evidence and applications
experimental prediction

A stated expected result that would follow if a proposed explanation and its assumptions were correct.

Review: Replication evidence
expressivity

The degree or form in which a genotype-associated trait appears among individuals who express it.

The second offspring generation, often produced by crossing F1 individuals in the stated model.

Review: Controlled crosses and evidence

The maximum expected recombinant fraction between two loci under the standard mapping model; larger map distances may be obscured by multiple crossovers.

Review: Limits of linkage estimates
folding

The process by which a polypeptide adopts a three-dimensional structure influenced by sequence and conditions.

Review: Reading the genetic code
four gamete types

The four allele combinations AB, Ab, aB and ab available from AaBb when the two loci assort independently.

Review: Dihybrid crosses
fragment size

The length of a DNA fragment, commonly measured in base pairs.

Review: Amplifying and separating

A reading-frame change caused by insertion or deletion of nucleotides not in a multiple of three within a coding region.

Review: Types of sequence change
Franklin

Rosalind Franklin, whose X-ray diffraction work provided important structural evidence for DNA.

Review: Evidence for hereditary material
fraternal twins

Twins arising from two separate fertilizations; they are also called dizygotic twins.

An experiment that tests how a variant, molecule, cell, or process performs rather than only detecting its presence.

A haploid reproductive cell—sperm or egg lineage cell—that can contribute one chromosome set at fertilization.

Review: Inheritance modes and notation
gametophyte

A multicellular haploid stage that produces gametes by mitosis in a plant life cycle.

Review: Comparing divisions

A method that separates charged molecules through a gel, commonly resolving DNA fragments mainly by length.

Review: Amplifying and separating
gene

A region of DNA whose information contributes to a functional RNA molecule or protein.

Review: DNA packaging

Tendency of loci on the same chromosome to be inherited together, especially when they are physically close.

gene order

The relative arrangement of loci along a chromosome inferred from recombination evidence or physical mapping.

An approach intended to treat a condition by altering genetic material or its delivery/expression in relevant cells.

Review: Applications and uncertainty
gene-environment interaction

A pattern in which the effect of a genotype differs across environments or the environmental effect differs across genotypes.

generation

A group or stage in a parent-to-offspring sequence, defined for the population being studied.

Review: Gamete development

A professional process supporting informed understanding and decisions about genetic information, testing, uncertainty, and family implications.

genetic privacy

Protection of identifiable genetic information from collection, access, or use without appropriate consent and governance.

genetic testing

Analysis of genetic material to investigate a specified variant or question, with limits determined by the method.

Review: Applications and uncertainty
genetic variation

Differences in DNA sequences or chromosome content among cells or organisms. Mutation can originate variants, and recombination can create new combinations; environment and development also affect phenotypes without necessarily changing inherited DNA.

Review: Comparing divisions
genotype

The probability of a specified allele combination under the assumptions of a genetic cross or population model.

The relative numbers or probabilities of specified genotype classes, written in a stated order; for example, AA:Aa:aa = 1:2:1.

Review: Monohybrid crosses

A model connecting genotype with possible phenotype while accounting for expression, development, environment, and variation.

germ-line mutation

A mutation in a gamete-producing lineage that can be transmitted to offspring.

Review: Inheritance and variation
goodness of fit

A comparison of observed category counts with counts expected under a stated model.

haploid

Having one chromosome set, conventionally written n.

Review: Sets and copies
haploid product

A cell containing one complete chromosome set after a specified division or life-cycle transition.

Review: First meiotic division

A life cycle in which the multicellular haploid stage is the main body and the diploid stage is brief.

helicase

An enzyme that separates paired DNA strands at a replication fork.

Review: Enzymes and direction

heteroplasmy

heterozygous

Review: Inheritance language
homologous chromosome

One of a pair of chromosomes with corresponding loci, one typically inherited from each parent, though alleles may differ.

homologous pair

Two chromosomes with corresponding gene positions, usually one inherited from each parent; they may carry different versions of the same genes.

Review: Sets and copies
homozygous

Having two copies of the same allele at a locus in a diploid cell or organism.

Review: Inheritance language

A noncovalent interaction contributing to the specificity and stability of paired DNA bases.

Review: Nucleotides and direction
hypothesis

A testable proposed explanation that generates evidence-based predictions.

identical twins

Twins arising when one early embryo separates into two; they are also called monozygotic twins and need not share every later trait.

incidental finding

A potentially meaningful result discovered outside the original purpose of an analysis or test.

independent assortment

Independent orientation and separation of different homologous chromosome pairs during meiosis, producing independent allele assortment for unlinked loci.

Review: Sources of variation
independent event

An event whose occurrence does not change the probability of another event under the stated model.

Review: Probability and test crosses

Events whose probabilities are unchanged by the outcomes of earlier trials under the model.

Review: Inheritance modes and notation
independent variable

The factor deliberately changed or used to define comparison groups in an investigation.

individual

One organism or labelled case in the stated population or pedigree.

Review: Reading karyotypes
inheritance model

A stated set of rules linking parental alleles, gametes and offspring genotypes/phenotypes.

Review: Controlled crosses and evidence
initiation

The assembly and starting stage of a process, such as translation at an appropriate start site.

Review: Enzymes and direction
insert

The DNA segment placed into a vector or other specified DNA construct.

Review: Cutting and joining DNA
insertion

Addition of one or more nucleotides or of a chromosome segment.

Review: Types of sequence change

The cell-cycle period including G1, S, and G2, when cells grow, function, replicate DNA, and prepare for division.

intron

A transcribed segment removed from a pre-mRNA during RNA splicing.

joint probability

The probability that two or more specified events occur together.

karyotype

An organized display or description of chromosomes used to examine number and large-scale structure.

Review: DNA packaging

A protein attachment structure at a chromosome’s centromere that connects it to spindle fibres.

Review: Preparing to separate
ladder

A set of DNA fragments of known sizes used as a gel reference.

Review: Amplifying and separating

The new DNA strand synthesized discontinuously as Okazaki fragments away from each advancing replication fork.

The new DNA strand synthesized continuously toward an advancing replication fork.

The sequence of developmental and reproductive stages connecting one generation with the next.

ligase

An enzyme that seals breaks in a DNA sugar-phosphate backbone by forming phosphodiester bonds.

Review: Enzymes and direction
likelihood

How compatible observed evidence is with a specified model or parameter value.

The probability of the observed evidence under one hypothesis divided by its probability under another hypothesis.

limitation

A boundary on what a method, dataset or model can establish.

Review: Preparing to separate
linked loci

Gene positions on the same chromosome; nearby positions tend to be inherited together because crossing over separates them less often.

Review: Sources of variation
locus

A defined chromosome position or DNA region used to locate a gene or marker.

Review: DNA packaging

A linkage-map distance equal to a one-percent recombination frequency; also called a centimorgan.

A usually free-swimming body form of some cnidarians; not all cnidarians have this stage.

Review: Sexual and asexual reproduction

A two-division process following one DNA replication that produces haploid cells and generates genetic variation.

A segregation error in the first division, such as homologues failing to separate normally.

The meiotic division in which sister chromatids separate without another preceding DNA replication.

A segregation error in the second division, such as sister chromatids failing to separate normally.

Review: Nondisjunction

An interval during which a meiotic process is arrested at a particular stage.

Review: Gamete development

An RNA molecule carrying a coding sequence from DNA transcription to a ribosome for translation.

A division stage in which chromosomes align near the middle of the cell with attachments to the spindle.

Review: Measuring cell populations
metaphase I

The meiotic stage when homologous chromosome pairs align before their separation.

Review: First meiotic division

A dynamic cytoskeletal polymer that forms much of the spindle and moves or positions chromosomes.

missense

A coding-sequence change that substitutes one amino acid for another in a protein.

Review: Reading the genetic code
mitochondrial DNA

DNA contained in mitochondria; its inheritance pattern differs from that of nuclear chromosomes in many organisms.

Inheritance of mitochondrial DNA, usually through the egg cytoplasm in humans, with effects influenced by heteroplasmy.

The proportion of observed cells that are in mitosis at a particular time.

Review: Measuring cell populations
model assumption

A stated condition required for a model's predictions or calculations to apply.

model calibration

Assessment of whether predicted probabilities match observed frequencies in an appropriate population.

monohybrid cross

A genetic cross that follows inheritance at one locus.

monosomy

Aneuploidy in which one chromosome from a pair is missing.

mosaicism

mRNA

An RNA molecule carrying a coding sequence from DNA transcription to a ribosome for translation.

A trait influenced by multiple genetic factors, environmental factors, and their interactions.

Two or more crossing-over events within the chromosome interval being studied.

A probability rule that multiplies probabilities along a sequence of independent or conditional events.

mutagen

An agent that can increase the chance of changes to genetic material.

Review: Effects on gene products
mutation

A change in DNA sequence that can create a new allele; whether it reaches offspring depends on the cell lineage and reproduction.

negative control

A comparison expected to lack the target signal, used to reveal contamination or background effects.

nondisjunction

Failure of homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids to separate during a cell division.

nondisjunction

nonsense

notation

The symbols and conventions used to represent biological quantities or relationships.

Review: Inheritance language

DNA contained in the nucleus, including the chromosomes used in ordinary nuclear inheritance models.

observed count

The number actually measured in a category before comparison with a model.

P generation

Review: Controlled crosses and evidence
P site

pairwise distance

An estimated separation between two gene loci, expressed in a stated mapping unit.

Review: Gene order

phenotype ratio

A chemical group in the nucleic-acid backbone that contributes to its negative charge and connections between sugars.

Rosalind Franklin and Raymond Gosling's X-ray diffraction image whose pattern provided important evidence about DNA's helical structure.

A photograph obtained through a microscope; it records actual observed material rather than a schematic drawing.

Review: Measuring cell populations
plasmid

A usually circular DNA molecule that replicates separately from a cell's main chromosome and can serve as a biotechnology vector.

ploidy

The number of complete chromosome sets in a cell or life-cycle stage.

A small haploid cell produced by unequal cytokinesis during oogenesis that usually does not become an egg.

A trait influenced by variation at many genetic loci, commonly also affected by environment.

polygenic trait

A trait influenced by variation at many genetic loci, commonly also affected by environment.

Review: Processing and expression
polyploid

Review: Sets and copies

A comparison expected to produce a known signal, used to show that a method can detect its target.

Control and appropriate protection of personal information, including genetic information.

Review: Reading karyotypes

A numerical measure of how likely an event is under a stated model, from zero to one.

A probability rule that multiplies probabilities along a sequence of independent or conditional events.

A molecule made of a chain or chains of small building blocks called amino acids; its sequence and folded shape help determine its function.

The idea that a mutation does not arise because the organism anticipates a useful outcome.

restriction enzyme

An enzyme that recognizes a particular DNA sequence and cuts the phosphodiester backbone at or near that site.

A map drawn in the opposite left-to-right direction while preserving the same gene order relationships and distances.

Review: Processing and expression
risk

Review: Many genes and environment
RNA

Ribonucleic acid: a molecule related to DNA whose chemical units usually use U instead of T; different RNAs carry information, help assemble proteins or carry out other cellular functions.

sample

Chance difference between a sample result and the underlying probabilities or population because only a finite sample was observed.

sampling variation

Chance difference between a sample result and the underlying probabilities or population because only a finite sample was observed.

substitution

Replacement of one nucleotide or chromosome segment with another.

Review: Reading karyotypes

A probability rule for mutually exclusive alternatives: add the probabilities of the separate outcomes.

trisomy

tRNA

An adaptor RNA carrying a specific amino acid and an anticodon that pairs with an mRNA codon.

James Watson, who worked with Francis Crick on a model of DNA structure informed by experimental evidence.

Describes a gene located on the X chromosome and its associated inheritance pattern.
